clue.text: Phone the doctor with venom

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
bile is bitter spite, like venom

explanation.surface: Someone rings a doctor about a poisonous bite.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is a standard crossword doctor; 'with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellphone is called this in British English, so the noun stands for a telephone you carry about.

clue.text: Deceive company into a restructure to get endorsement

parts.note: to con is to deceive or swindle
a firm is a business company

indicators.note: a restructure reorganises, so the letters of the words 'into a' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm is tricked into reorganising so as to win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a container signal, but it is part of what 'restructure' rearranges, giving the last five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A confirmation is a formal endorsement or ratification of something.

clue.text: A patient analysis?

parts.note: reads as a careful, unhurried study, but means the write-up of one patient's medical case

explanation.definitionFit: A detailed study of one example, originally a single medical patient's history, is this kind of report.

clue.text: Deny no-one outside access

indicators.note: the outside of the word no-one means just its first and last letters

parts.note: a gate is a way in, an access point

explanation.surface: Nobody is refused entry from outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny or nullify a claim or effect.

clue.text: Background notes to film

parts.note: looks like explanatory notes about a movie, but means musical notes played behind the action of a film

explanation.definitionFit: Music composed to accompany a play or film, in the background of the action, has this name.

clue.text: Cathedral welcomes one member of the government

indicators.note: a building that welcomes someone takes them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a minster is a large church or cathedral, such as York Minster
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cathedral receives a visiting politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister heads a department, so is one member of the government.

clue.text: Discrimination makes sense

definitions.meaning: discernment in judging what is fine or fitting
one of the five senses, perceiving flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Good judgment in style is called this, and it is also the faculty of perceiving flavour.

clue.text: Proposal to provide introductory notes

definitions.meaning: an approach or offer made to someone
the orchestral piece played before an opera

explanation.definitionFit: An opening offer in negotiation has this name, as does the instrumental opening of an opera.

clue.text: Seating available up to now has no back

indicators.note: having no back means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: so far means up to the present time

explanation.surface: A seat that has been available until now lacks a backrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no back' removes the final R of SO FAR; 'available' is padding linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is an item of seating furniture for several people.

clue.text: Container or stein designed to be carried in vehicle

indicators.note: something carried in a vehicle sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: designed means made up anew, so the letters of stein are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin or a beer mug is made to be transported in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stein' is a beer mug, which suits the container picture, but here it is only letters for 'designed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a cylindrical metal container for tea, film or the like.

clue.text: The intelligentsia invest it in retail trade

indicators.note: to invest something in another is to put it inside, so one piece is placed within the other
to trade is to exchange, so the letters of retail are swapped about

explanation.surface: Intellectuals are urged to put money into shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' reads as a money word to suit 'retail', but signals placing one piece inside the rearranged other.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are learned, literary people: the intellectual class.

clue.text: Gets wind of American cash being loaded on board ship

indicators.note: cargo loaded on board goes inside the vessel, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
cents are units of US money

explanation.surface: Someone hears a rumour about dollars being stowed on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent something is to detect it by smell, so figuratively to get wind of it.

clue.text: Payment made for subsidence

definitions.meaning: the paying off of a bill or debt
the gradual sinking of a building

explanation.definitionFit: Paying a debt is called this, and so is a building's sinking into its foundations.

clue.text: More French perhaps?

parts.note: the French word for 'again' or 'more', and also what an audience shouts for an extra piece

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for 'again' is used in English for an extra performance demanded by the audience.

clue.text: Policeman gets errant criminal as colleague

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters of errant are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer is paired with a wayward lawbreaker as a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A copartner shares in a business or venture, so is a colleague.

clue.text: Source of revenue in ship's flag

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the ship

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: Money comes from a vessel's flag, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of revenue' looks like a phrase such as 'stream', but it is just R, put inside STEAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant flown from a mast.

clue.text: Out of bed and into a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone gets up and is sent straight to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astir means up and moving about, having got out of bed.

clue.text: Song about a leader of Africa being a curse

indicators.note: about means around, so the song goes round the a

parts.note: an anthem is a song, such as a national song

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A song about an African leader amounts to a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, or something detested.

clue.text: Don't leave the street area over there

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
yon is an old word meaning that place over there

explanation.surface: An instruction not to quit the neighbourhood over yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain somewhere rather than leave.

clue.text: Jack is fit to crew on the Mediterranean

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after

parts.note: able means fit or capable
the Mediterranean is a sea
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A sailor is fit to serve on a vessel in the Med.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (as in Jack Tar) is a traditional name for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a rank of sailor, and jack is old slang for any sailor.

clue.text: Unhappy getting led off to seat

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable being led away to a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is the seat on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Broadcaster obtaining a release

parts.note: to untie is to free or release

explanation.surface: A radio station secures a person's freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC, the UK's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately nicknamed by this family word for a father's or mother's sister.

clue.text: A tyrant needs to look after the lower socio-economic groups

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: D and E are the lowest British social grades
to spot is to see or look

explanation.surface: A dictator ought to care for the poorest people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look after' reads as 'care for', but splits into a synonym and a placing word; D and E are the UK market-research grades for the lowest-income groups.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler, a tyrant.

clue.text: Media campaign

explanation.definitionFit: Journalists collectively go by this name, and to urge a cause hard is to campaign for it.

clue.text: Modernising university with little money, and going steady

parts.note: P is a penny, a small amount of British money
dating means going out with someone regularly

explanation.surface: A student with little cash and a regular partner is moving with the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Updating something brings it up to date, making it modern.

clue.text: School master accepts the compiler gets current measures on them

indicators.note: accepting something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other
to school is to train or reshape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A headmaster takes on the setter, who gets the measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun qualifying the next word, but it is the anagram signal applied after 'accepts' has done its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammeters are instruments that measure electric current in amperes.

clue.text: Put out by the hour going back

indicators.note: going back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the hour is the time

explanation.surface: Something is extinguished as the clocks go back.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, so to put out.

clue.text: Shout, getting furious at callers, it's obvious

parts.note: cry means shout

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so the letters of at callers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone yells angrily at visitors, plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' seems to describe the shouting, but it signals rearranging the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crystal-clear is completely transparent, so perfectly obvious.
